accounting.rationale: PDF130 defines INTRINSIC procedure identity and three name-role possibilities. These are not a requirement for every intrinsic reference to have an explicit declaration or a new no-op classifier.
Intrinsic procedure identity is distinct from an external procedure using the same spelling. C842, C1522 and4.2p2(7) retain their attribute/name/nonstandard-intrinsic owners.
Generic intrinsic names and their argument keyword/class information are16.7. Generic name alone does not make a procedure eligible as an actual argument.
16.8 distinguishes unrestricted Table16.2 names from restricted Table16.3 names, with argument type/kind and result-characteristic conditions.

Some spellings have both roles. In an eligible procedure-actual context, the specific procedure is associated under15.5.2.10p4; generic overload resolution is not substituted for its specified characteristics.

The explicit-attribute obligation is separate from the inline reminder of the Table16.3 exclusion, whose numbered owner isC1534. Declaring INTRINSIC is necessary in the stated use but does not make every intrinsic eligible.
Map the restricted-specific exclusion to15.5.1 C1534/16.8 Table16.3; do not create a second rejection requirement or infer permission for pointer targets/interfaces from actual-argument eligibility.
The parenthetical C1534 reference identifies the canonical owner and its required diagnostic basis. Future reuse is separately adjudicated, not automatically credited.

requirements.title: A shared explicit intrinsic generic and accessible generic interfaces agree on procedure class
requirements.definition: When an intrinsic generic name is explicitly declared INTRINSIC and is also the name of one or more generic interfaces accessible in the same scoping unit, the intrinsic generic and every procedure in those interfaces must all be functions or all be subroutines. The explicit declaration, shared generic identity, accessibility and scope conditions are retained.

pending.function-extension-control: PENDING a complete explicit INTRINSIC generic function extended by an independently distinguishable user function. Match actual procedure class and16.7 intrinsic characteristics; a result-type change alone is not the definition of distinguishability. Use one unambiguous specific at first.
pending.subroutine-extension-control: PENDING a corresponding intrinsic generic subroutine and compatible-class user subroutine, with a genuinely distinguishable interface. Declaration admission does not prescribe a random-number, timing, I/O or other intrinsic runtime result.
pending.intrinsic-function-subroutine-conflict: PENDING an explicitly declared intrinsic generic function with a same-name accessible user generic containing an otherwise valid singleton subroutine. Establish a complete minimal class-consistent repair and exact diagnostic cause before implementation; do not silently rely on removing INTRINSIC while an independent generic-class violation remains.
pending.intrinsic-subroutine-function-conflict: PENDING the reverse class conflict, starting from a real standard intrinsic generic subroutine and an otherwise valid user function. Keep signature, visibility and declaration order valid; an unsupported intrinsic name or malformed interface cannot qualify.
pending.multiple-accessible-interfaces: PENDING local and use/host-accessible generic-interface contexts with more than one nonintrinsic specific, retaining all pairwise distinguishability rules and exact scope/identity. A private specific name can still contribute through an accessible generic under15.4.3.4.5p1.
pending.explicit-premise-and-C1514-source: PENDING the precise relation to C1514's general same-class and distinguishability requirements. Record overlapping causes rather than claiming a heterogeneous user-only interface isolates C850. Absence of explicit INTRINSIC is not assumed to repair every conflicting generic relationship.

requirements.oracle: Complete homogeneous-class controls and source-qualified cross-class negatives, with exact generic identity, accessible scope and independently valid repairs. C1514 overlap remains an explicit causal-analysis gate.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required reporting capability does not mandate fatal exit, specific English or a printed constraint code. Generic ambiguity, unsupported intrinsic facilities, duplicate unrelated entities, missing interfaces and native compiler failures are not interchangeable with the class mismatch.

requirements.title: A specific intrinsic used as an actual argument requires explicit INTRINSIC specification
requirements.definition: When a specific intrinsic name is used as an actual argument, it must be explicitly specified INTRINSIC. Eligibility remains restricted to the allowed specific intrinsic functions and compatible dummy-procedure characteristics. The attribute is not a way to pass a generic-only name, a Table16.3 restricted specific or any arbitrarily named procedure.

pending.allowed-specific-actual: PENDING a complete explicitly declared Table16.2 specific such as default-INTEGER IABS passed to a compatible dummy procedure. Any callback has independently derived INTEGER results, multiple meaningful invocations and valid characteristics; the elemental-intrinsic actual exception does not make the dummy elemental.
pending.generic-specific-name-overlap: PENDING a Table16.2 spelling that is also generic, retaining its table-specified argument type/kind and16.8 result rules when used as a procedure actual. Do not choose another generic overload from the receiver's desired signature or guess nondefault-kind availability.
pending.explicit-declaration-mechanisms: PENDING the exact15.4.3.7/R1519 INTRINSIC-statement and8.2 attribute-declaration relations under their actual type/entity restrictions. An EXTERNAL statement or PROCEDURE declaration is not an INTRINSIC substitute; preserve C842 and C1522 ownership.
pending.restricted-specific-canonical-owner: PENDING a separately reviewed source/use relation to15.5.1 C1534 and16.8 Table16.3. The explicit attribute cannot legalize a restricted actual. Pointer-target, initialization-target and interface exclusions remain C1033/C1519/C1515, not extra coverage inferred from this actual-argument requirement.
pending.other-intrinsic-context-boundaries: PENDING direct intrinsic calls, intrinsic-module procedures and generic-only names under their own declaration/import/interface rules. This paragraph's specific-actual condition is not a blanket explicit-INTRINSIC requirement for every ordinary intrinsic invocation.
pending.missing-declaration-reporting-source: PENDING exact4.2p2 numbered/scope/nonstandard-intrinsic reporting analysis for a proposed missing-declaration contrast. The prose shall alone supplies no universal rejection obligation; an implicit variable/type error or unrelated C1534 exclusion is not the same cause.

requirements.oracle: Meaningful eligible specific-procedure positive controls and finite declaration/eligibility source relations. Specific characteristics and callback results come from the standard, not compiler agreement.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No compulsory S-level rejection without a separate diagnostic basis, no arbitrary generic dispatch through a specific actual and no new intrinsic-result effect owner. Canonical witness roles are preserved; unsupported relationship mechanisms stay pending.

review_rationale: Independent original-source review87efa687790ffb131c1952cf92b57242d479db5969c23a96c58c64a41c3755e2, registered in doc/source_audits/batch_054.json. All3base/15fine units and two requirements retain12pending facets. Generic/specific/shared intrinsic names and Table16.2eligibility/characteristics are distinct; explicit INTRINSIC does not legalize Table16.3actuals. C1534 remains the external canonical owner. C850 preserves explicit declaration, shared accessible same-scope generic identity and all-function/all-subroutine conditions, with C1514/distinguishability and valid-repair gates. Prose missing-declaration rejection is not automatically required. No fixture or connection is approved.
